_comment: Retrieval gate thresholds. One entry per (profile, benchmark, split).
Each entry records the measured baseline it was derived from, the
thresholds set below it, and when it was measured. The rule for the
thresholds is the same one the v2 dev gate already used:
rounded DOWN to two decimals. The margin absorbs corpus growth; it
is not slack for a regression. A threshold is never set at or above
its baseline, and an existing gate's thresholds are never raised
to make a failing run pass.
Each gate is derived INDEPENDENTLY from the baseline of the split
it scores. The held_out thresholds are NOT the dev thresholds:
held_out is a harder split, so its baselines are lower and its
thresholds are correspondingly lower. Reusing the dev thresholds
on held_out would fail on current code and prove nothing.
'local' is the MiniLM profile: free, offline, deterministic, and
what CI builds. '3large' is the production default (ADR-016); its
gates need an OpenRouter key and a 3072-dim index, so they are not
run by the default CI job. See notes/2026-10-28-default-embedder-3large.md.

note: The historical gate. The v1 benchmark's 204 expected citations are
all Bible, so it is scoped to Christianity: unscoped, the 3-tradition
index dilutes it to 0.234, which measures scope, not retrieval.
Thresholds are unchanged since 2026-09-11.
The cross-tradition gate. 48 dev queries whose 229 expected citations
span Christianity (111), Tanakh (73) and Quran (45), unscoped so all
three traditions are searchable. Unchanged since 2026-10-25.
The held-out gate. 42 queries that the dev thresholds were never
tuned against. Its own baselines are much lower than dev's
(semantic 0.106 vs 0.189), which is the correct signal: the local
embedder adds little over BM25 on the harder split. Applying the
dev thresholds here would fail on current code.
These thresholds are derived from these baselines with the same
0.04 margin the dev gate uses. They are NOT the dev thresholds.
Held-out is a measurement split, not a tuning split. Thresholds are
derived from its baselines and then frozen; they are not adjusted
in response to what the gate reports, which is what would turn a
held-out split into a second dev split.
The production default profile's gate (ADR-016). Measured against
the COMPLETE 66,689 x 3072 index. The 2026-10-26 number for this
profile (0.344) was void: that index held only 30,159 vectors and
was Christianity-only. See notes/2026-10-26-truncated-index-found.md.
BM25 is identical to the local gate's (0.119) because BM25 does not
use the embedder. That equality is the internal control showing the
benchmark, corpus and scorer were the same in both arms.
Requires an OpenRouter key and a 3072-dim index. Not run by the
default CI job; see the ADR for why.
